name: hirokata
description: A curated collection of Claude Code plugins for enhanced development workflows

plugins.name: software
plugins.description: Requirements-to-implementation workflow with 8-phase clean architecture, automated planning, adaptive parallel execution, intelligent conventional commit generation, and comprehensive requirements documentation.

plugins.name: guild
plugins.description: Continuous agent orchestration where the plugin IS a schema and a set of skills — there is no CLI. `tursodb` already executes SQL, so guild members reach the board by writing their own SQL against a guide, and the guild's rules live IN the database: CHECK constraints are the status vocabularies, VIEWS are the derived rules (the cursor, the review gate, node readiness, the matcher, the board, the brief — each with ONE definition, so two members cannot get two answers), and TRIGGERS write the `event` record on every mutation. A member can forget to call a command; a member cannot bypass a trigger or a CHECK. A ticket names a required CAPABILITY rather than an agent, so adding an agent file is the whole of hiring. Each requirement runs an execution graph with exactly two gates — the plan is approved before anything is built, and findings, bugs and failures are presented together as one decision after review — and it can work a shift unattended, stopping at the next gate because a gate is the one decision no subagent can make. An independent QA discipline files bugs and maps risk coverage as rows. Say 'check in' to start a work session, or 'work a shift' to leave it running. v6 is a fresh rewrite: the v5 CLI's test suite and review rounds do not carry over to code that no longer exists.

plugins.name: research
plugins.description: PhD-level multi-perspective research inspired by Stanford's STORM. The 'storm research' skill orchestrates five expert persona agents (practitioner, skeptic, economist, historian, academic), maps their contradictions, synthesizes a cited briefing, and red-teams the result. Say 'storm research <topic>' to start.

plugins.name: storytelling
plugins.description: Turn any idea, pitch, update, or decision into a message that lands using six proven storytelling frameworks (Simon Sinek's Golden Circle, Minto's Pyramid Principle, the Pixar Pitch, StoryBrand, What/So What/Now What, and ABT). The 'storytelling' skill diagnoses your audience and goal, recommends the right framework, and drafts the message — in parallel across frameworks when the framing is uncertain. Each framework is also a standalone skill. Say 'help me tell the story of <X>' to start.
